comparison: Perfect agreement on C1-C10. Both evaluations find the nucleolar morphology characterization well-supported. Peer reviewers specifically praise this as 'the strength of this study' and note it provides 'convincing evidence' for Treacle's scaffolding function in FC formation.

Both address transcription claims (C11-C13 in OpenEval; C11-C15 in peer review). OpenEval finds ChIP-qPCR data supports reduced but not absent transcription factor binding. Peer review provides 'convincing evidence' for Treacle's necessity in rRNA transcription, accepting these functional claims without challenge.

OpenEval evaluates C14-C15 (transcription suppression data) as supported by EU incorporation and RT-qPCR. Peer review R2 covers broader transcription claims (C11-C15) and accepts the functional evidence for Treacle's role in transcription.

Perfect agreement on C16-C21. Both accept the structural characterization of Treacle domains. OpenEval notes computational predictions and literature support. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this by discussing 'the charge-segregated central region' without challenge.

Both address in vitro condensation (C22-C24), but with different evaluations. OpenEval finds the data strongly supportive of LLPS capacity. Peer review expresses uncertainty, noting 'all proteins will condense at sufficiently high concentrations' and questioning whether 100μM protein with 5% PEG8000 demonstrates physiological relevance.

OpenEval evaluates C25-C26 (optogenetic condensation) as supported. Peer review R5 covers broader cellular condensation claims (C25-C33) and accepts the in vivo data, with Reviewer 1 specifically praising 'overexpression studies done in the absence of endogenous protein.'

OpenEval evaluates C27-C31 (cellular condensate morphology and controls) as well-supported. Peer review R5 accepts cellular condensation broadly (C25-C33), with the editor noting the study 'reveals that Treacle undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation in vitro and in vivo.'

OpenEval evaluates C32-C33 (fusion events) as supported by time-lapse imaging. Peer review R5 covers these claims within broader cellular condensation acceptance (C25-C33), with Reviewer 3 noting 'high quality' data and 'well-designed' experiments.

Perfect agreement on C34-C40. Both accept FRAP characterization of condensate dynamics. OpenEval notes comprehensive analysis across multiple conditions. Peer review accepts dynamic properties as part of condensation characterization without challenge.

OpenEval evaluates C41-C42 (N-terminal domain dispensability) as supported. Peer review R7 covers broader deletion mutant analysis (C41-C52) and praises the 'ambitious and critical' separation-of-function mutant approach.

Both address RD deletion effects (C43-C48). OpenEval finds the data supports critical role of RD in proper condensation. Peer review accepts this as part of the praised separation-of-function mutant analysis providing 'new insight into the charge-segregated central region.'

OpenEval evaluates C49-C51 (CD deletion effects) as supported. Peer review R7 encompasses these claims in broader acceptance of deletion mutant studies (C41-C52), viewing the domain dissection as a strength of the work.

Both address synthesis of deletion mutant findings. OpenEval evaluates C52, C71-C74 as supported cooperative model. Peer review R10 specifically highlights 'the charge scramble mutant' characterization, accepting the charge-based mechanistic model.

Perfect agreement on C53-C58. Both accept that electrostatic interactions drive condensation. OpenEval notes convergence of in vitro and in vivo results. Peer review explicitly accepts 'condensation in a manner that depends on concentration and charge-charge interactions.'

OpenEval evaluates C59-C61 (S/E-rich LCR role) as supported. Peer review R9 covers these within broader acceptance of charge-based dissection (C59-C67), part of the praised separation-of-function mutant analysis.

Strong agreement on C62-C67. OpenEval finds dual role of K-rich LCR well-supported. Peer review accepts this fine-mapping as part of 'ambitious and critical' mutant analysis, with Reviewer 2 specifically highlighting charge scramble mutant effects.

Both address charge scrambling experiment (C68-C70). OpenEval praises this as 'sophisticated experimental design' supporting diblock ampholyte model. Peer review R10 specifically highlights charge scramble mutant characterization as a strength, accepting mechanistic implications.

OpenEval evaluates C75-C79 (altered interactions of condensation-defective mutants) as supported. Peer review R11 accepts these altered interaction patterns (C75-C86), noting mutants 'de-mix FBL from the DFC.'

Strong agreement on C80-C86. OpenEval finds correlation between condensation defects and altered protein partnerships well-documented. Peer review accepts that condensation mediates proper organization, with findings 'tie to a role in maintaining separation of FC components from the DFC.'

Both address transcription defects in condensation-defective mutants (C87-C91). OpenEval finds correlation well-established. Peer review provides 'convincing evidence' that condensation is necessary for transcription, noting mutants 'lower pre-rRNA synthesis.'

Strong agreement on C92-C98. OpenEval finds smFISH data supports loss of spatial organization and processing defects. Peer review accepts that condensation-defective mutants are 'disrupted in supporting Treacle's functions in rDNA transcription and rRNA processing.'

Both address TOPBP1 interaction (C99-C101). OpenEval finds convergence of multiple techniques provides strong evidence. Peer review accepts the basic finding but notes 'further studies will be required to fully explore the relevance of Treacle condensation to the stability of the rDNA repeats.'
Both address condensation-dependence of TOPBP1 interaction (C102-C103). OpenEval praises rescue experiment design. Peer review accepts the interaction data as part of broader DDR findings (C99-C107).

Strong agreement on C104-C107. OpenEval finds DDR marker analysis demonstrates phase separation requirement. Peer review provides 'convincing evidence' for Treacle's necessity in rDNA repair, noting mutants 'abolish the recruitment of TOPBP1.'

OpenEval evaluates C108-C110 (Treacle as FC scaffold) as supported by current study integrated with literature. Peer review R14 accepts broader mechanistic interpretations (C108-C128), viewing the study as 'important for understanding Treacle in nucleolar organization.'

OpenEval evaluates C111-C115 (RD-CD cooperation model) as well-supported, noting zebrafish comparison relies on cited work. Peer review accepts these mechanistic interpretations as part of broader narrative about condensation principles.

Both address mechanistic model of charge interactions (C116-C125). OpenEval notes some aspects are speculative but well-reasoned. Peer review accepts these interpretations as part of the overall narrative without specific challenge.

OpenEval rates C126-C128 as UNCERTAIN, noting PTM effects on condensation are speculative without direct experimental evidence. Peer review R14 accepts broader mechanistic discussion (C108-C128) but does not specifically evaluate the PTM speculation.

Strong agreement on C129-C134. OpenEval finds the model linking FC/DFC disorganization to processing defects reasonable. Peer review accepts the integrated functional model, noting 'findings integrate well towards a compelling narrative.'

OpenEval evaluates C135-C139 (DDR mechanism beyond phosphorylation) as supported and representing important mechanistic advance. Peer review accepts DDR findings (C99-C107) but notes further studies needed to fully explore condensation relevance to rDNA stability.

Both accept C140 as overarching conclusion. OpenEval finds it well-supported by comprehensive demonstration of multiple functions. Peer review accepts the integrated hub protein concept, with editor noting the study demonstrates necessity for 'rRNA transcription, and rDNA repair.'
